intro: The analysis below summarizes the performance of candidates in the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 6 October 2026 across the reported shifts. Shift 1 showed mixed performance with no overall difficulty rating, while Shift 2 was reported as easy across all sections. Shift 3 has not been conducted yet, and its analysis will be added after the shift. All figures presented are unofficial; the SSC normalises scores across shifts for final reporting.

shifts.summary: The shift 1 paper showed mixed performance across sections. Candidates attempted around 80‑90 questions, with accuracy varying by source. Reasoning contained geometry, number series and coding‑decoding items, while GA focused on constitutional articles and sports. Quantitative section emphasized trigonometry, arithmetic and geometry, and English had easy comprehension and spelling items. Observed issues included timer problems and travel costs.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning was reported as relatively high with some puzzle and number‑series questions skipped due to time. Mix of analogy, coding‑decoding and statement‑based items. Some reports mention a cuboid question and lengthy slog patterns.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GK mix of static and current‑affairs questions, many on constitutional articles and sports. Some reports note few current affairs and close options. Topics also included committees, economics index and historical facts.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quantitative section had many lengthy calculations, with advanced arithmetic and trigonometry dominating. Time shortage caused skips in mensuration and geometry problems. Reports vary on difficulty from easy to difficult.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English featured easy comprehension passages and spelling‑heavy items. Grammar and vocabulary questions were also present. Overall section reported as easy to moderate.

asked.q: Sin θ, cos θ, compound interest, ceiling, discount

observations: Candidates reported high travel cost due to distant centre locations.
Sectional timer caused problems, especially in the Math section.
Paper length was less than previous attempts.
Some out‑of‑syllabus questions appeared, such as a cuboid problem in reasoning.
disagreements: Overall difficulty reported from Easy to Difficult across sources.
Overall good attempts varied from 78 to 97 and 85 out of 100.
Reasoning difficulty described as Easy, Moderate, or not reported.
Quantitative difficulty described as Easy, Difficult, and Moderate.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 6 October 2026?
